subject: Stage-gate SLO readout and POC action plan
messages:
From: Erin Caldwell <erin@stratusai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + ask: defining POC success metrics and timeline

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the time. We left with a clear desire to run a short POC to validate latency and quality against our production prompt mix. A few asks so we can align on a concrete plan:

- Can you propose a concise SLO matrix we can evaluate against (latency/throughput/cost/quality)?
- What ownership will Redwood expect from our side (data, sample queries, evaluation rubric, TLS/KMS requirements)?
- Proposed timeline: we are targeting a 3-4 week hands-on trial starting mid-August. Is that feasible?

I've attached our internal POC checklist (attachment: poc_success_template.xlsx - spreadsheet) and shared two sample end-to-end queries in the doc. If you can sketch an acceptance gate and what success looks like, we can review with procurement/legal.

Two high-level constraints: we need p95 latency under 700ms for conversational flows and total inference cost to be < $0.003 per token if possible. We'll bring a small evaluation cohort (approx 1000 queries/day) for the trial.

Next steps: a short reply with the SLO proposal and owners would be great — Erin & Mike will consolidate on our side and return a signed SOW once we agree.

Best,
Erin
Erin Caldwell
Head of AI Engineering, StratusAI
(attachment: poc_success_template.xlsx)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Erin Caldwell <erin@stratusai.com>, Mike Zhou <mike.z@stratusai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: defining POC success metrics and timeline

Thanks Erin — great to meet you both. Draft SLO matrix and proposed responsibilities below. I've attached a short readme that maps our metrics to the evaluation steps (attachment: slo_readme.pdf).

High-level proposal (POC duration: 4 weeks):
- Acceptance gates (stage-gate):
  1) Integration & smoke (week 0-0.5): service reachable, TLS/KMS verified, sample requests run. Owner: Stratus (sample dataset), Redwood (integration runbook).
  2) Performance baseline (week 1): run controlled workload for latency/throughput. Gate: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 650ms on your sample mix. Owner: Redwood infra.
  3) Cost & scaling check (week 2): measure tokens/day and cost/token with our recommend batching/quantization. Gate: cost/token <= $0.0035 (we'll optimize toward $0.003). Owner: Redwood + Ben (cost modeling).
  4) Quality validation (week 3-4): blind evaluation vs your baseline model. Gate: top-line quality metric >= 90% (see rubric), no regression on critical intents. Owner: Stratus (human review) + Redwood (evaluation harness).

Detailed KPIs we want to track:
- Latency: p50, p90, p95 measured end-to-end (network + inference) on representative prompts.
- Throughput: sustained qps at target concurrency (you noted ~500 rps for peak flows).
- Cost: $/token with current config + an optimized run. We'll provide 1 representative day traffic profile.
- Quality: intent accuracy, slot F1 for extraction tasks, and a small sample of human-rated responses (N=300) for semantic correctness.

Operational notes and asks from Stratus: sample_queries.jsonl (please provide anonymized examples), account for tokenization differences, embargoed data handling (we support bringing data into a VPC if needed).

Action items (next 3 business days):
- Priya: send sample evaluation harness and default metrics dashboard (done: link in attachment).
- Jordan: prepare a quick cost estimate for 4-week run (attachment: cost_estimate_v1.xlsx).
- Erin/Mike: confirm sample dataset availability and preferred start window (mid-August ok?).

If that looks reasonable I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to lock timeline and legal asks.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: slo_readme.pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Caldwell <erin@stratusai.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: defining POC success metrics and timeline

Adding a few technical clarifications and an evaluation suggestion.

Thanks for the sample targets — two quick notes:
- Quality measurement: we recommend a two-track evaluation: (A) automated metrics (intent accuracy, slot F1) on a held-out labeled set, and (B) blind human rating of N=300 responses using a 1-5 rubric (precision/recall/fluency). We'll provide the scoring harness and an anonymized grading sheet.
- Baseline: what's your incumbent model & configs? If you can share the exact prompts and baseline outputs for ~500 queries, we can compute delta and show confidence intervals.
- Cost assumptions: cost/token varies with batching and sequence length. In our cost_estimate_v1.xlsx I've outlined three configs (no-quant, 4-bit, 8-bit) and estimated $/token for each. Expect us to iterate to meet your target of ~$0.003.

A short runbook for the performance run (week 1):
- Redwood prepares synthetic replay that mirrors your traffic distribution (we'll need a 24-hour sample).
- Run 3x ten-minute sustained windows at target concurrency (collect p50/p95/p99).
- Capture KV cache hit rates and any OOM/GC events.

Please see reply below for Priya's plan.

Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: defining POC success metrics and timeline

This all looks good — appreciate the clarity. Confirming the following: 

- We accept the 4-week cadence and the stage-gate approach. Start window: target kickoff week of Aug 16 — we will confirm by 7/20 after procurement check.
- We'll provide: anonymized sample_queries.jsonl (expected by 7/23), baseline outputs for 500 queries, and a list of redacted PII fields.
- Human evaluation: Stratus will field 2 raters for the initial batch and provide labels back to Redwood for analysis.
- Legal/procurement: once we finalize the SLO gates we'll route SOW to legal — expecting 5 business days after SOW sent.

Questions: can Redwood commit to an emergency fallback policy if the p95 spikes above 1200ms during the trial (i.e., automatic scale-up or model fallback)? Also, can you provide a short SLA note we can pass to procurement?

We'll wait for Jordan's cost estimate and Priya's harness link. If you can get the SOW template in the next 48 hours that will accelerate procurement on our side.

Thanks again — Erin
